packages.title: DESNZ Conversion factors 2026 voluntary Code of Practice statement — scope and status QA
facts: The voluntary compliance statement for the 2026 conversion factors was published on 11 June 2026.
It describes the Code of Practice pillars as Trustworthiness, Quality and Value.
The conversion factors are published annually by the Greenhouse Gas Inventory team in DESNZ.
The statement concerns statistical-production quality and does not itself provide parcel emissions measurements.
Method and publication-year context must remain attached to any factor-based calculation.

packages.title: Defra Farm Practices Survey February 2026 — scope and status QA
facts: Defra published the Farm Practices Survey February 2026 on 11 June 2026.
The survey applies to England and covers farming practices affected by agricultural and environmental issues.
The publication contains headline results and a time series containing data from 2011.
Survey responses describe practices and attitudes rather than measured greenhouse-gas mass at individual parcels.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from the survey.

packages.title: Defra Farm Practices Survey February 2026: Emissions — scope and status QA
facts: In 2026, 54% of farms surveyed considered greenhouse gases fairly or very important when making decisions about land, crops and livestock.
In 2026, 47% of farms surveyed were actively implementing measures to lower their emissions.
Among holdings taking action, recycling farm waste and improving energy efficiency were the two most popular reported actions.
Two percent of farms reported regularly feeding methane-suppressing feed products to livestock.
These are survey response percentages and are not measured greenhouse-gas emissions for individual land parcels.

packages.title: Defra Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025: Chapter 11 Agri-environment — scope and status QA
facts: Defra updated the Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025 agri-environment chapter on 10 July 2026.
The chapter covers emissions, pesticide use, fertiliser use, soil nutrient balances and revisions.
It reports that estimated greenhouse-gas and air-pollution emissions from agriculture fell 15% between 1990 and 2024.
The reported change is an agricultural-sector estimate, not a parcel measurement.
Revision status and the 1990 to 2024 reference period must be preserved.

packages.title: DfT Road traffic estimates in Great Britain: 2025 — scope and status QA
facts: DfT published Road traffic estimates in Great Britain: 2025 on 20 May 2026.
Motor vehicle traffic on Great Britain's roads was estimated at 342.6 billion vehicle miles in 2025.
The 2025 estimate was 1.9% higher than 2024.
The release provides estimates by vehicle type and road type for Great Britain and England.
Vehicle miles are activity statistics and are not direct greenhouse-gas measurements for road-adjacent parcels.

packages.title: DfT Road traffic estimates 2025: Traffic on England's road networks — scope and status QA
facts: DfT published the 2025 England road-network traffic release on 20 May 2026.
It covers annual 2025 traffic estimates for England's strategic and local road networks.
Annual traffic estimates use around 7,000 roadside 12-hour manual counts together with automatic traffic counters and road-length data.
The next annual release is expected in May 2027 for 2026 traffic figures.
Road-network traffic estimates do not establish parcel greenhouse-gas emissions.

packages.title: DfT Provisional road traffic estimates, Great Britain: April 2025 to March 2026 — scope and status QA
facts: DfT published provisional road traffic estimates for the year ending March 2026 on 25 June 2026.
The provisional estimate is 343.2 billion motor-vehicle miles in Great Britain for the year ending March 2026.
This was 2.0% higher than the year ending March 2025.
The release separates vehicle types and road classes and is explicitly provisional.
Provisional road activity must not be presented as final or as direct parcel emissions.
